title: Signal-detection replication of labels and literacy guide
why: Fixes the measurement failure: collects item-level real/AI judgments plus a confidence rating so d' and criterion can be estimated (U1), and gives a clean replication of the two nominal effects (U2).

power_target.basis: H1 observed 0.044 (Automated Flagging) shrunk toward the 0.03 MDE of the largest arm (0.0318 at n=333); a 3-point gain at 80% power needs roughly 420 per arm.

rationale: The source study found Automated Flagging raised accuracy 4.4 points (CI 1.4 to 7.3) and the AI Literacy Guide 4.7 points (CI 0.2 to 9.2), but pooled accuracy was only 1 point (CI -0.3 to 2.4) across 44 uncorrected tests. Only share-correct scores were stored, so sensitivity and response bias could not be separated, and Breathing and Nudge arms raised AI detection without raising authentic recognition.
contribution: Estimates d' and criterion separately for the two nominally effective interventions in a powered, preregistered replication with item-level data.
hypothesis: Automated labels and the literacy guide raise d' relative to control; if the effects are only criterion shifts, d' will not differ and c will move toward more AI responses.
primary_outcome: Sensitivity d' and criterion c from a multilevel signal-detection model (probit mixed model of AI judgment on true item status, arm, and their interaction, with random effects for respondent and item).
comparison: Each treatment arm versus control on d' and c; Holm correction across the two primary d' contrasts; criterion contrasts secondary; within-arm flagged versus unflagged items exploratory.
unresolved: The 40 image files, their ground-truth labels and the detector label assets must be supplied by the research team.
IRB approval number and participant compensation must be supplied.
The treatment block for the control arm is intentionally empty; the label arm's flags are shown inside the item stimuli.
label: Design advance

title: Does label benefit depend on stimulus difficulty and AI familiarity?
why: Addresses the missing moderator: E2 was empty and underpowered, and the high-familiarity halves have n=38 or fewer in some arms.

power_target.basis: H1 Automated Flagging 0.044, with a halved interaction detectable only with several hundred per cell.

rationale: Automated Flagging raised accuracy by 4.4 points (p=0.004) in the source study, but the familiarity heterogeneity table (E2) was empty and some high-familiarity arm halves had n=38 or fewer. This follow-up tests whether the gain holds across easy vs hard stimuli and across prior AI familiarity, with enough power for an interaction test.
contribution: Tests whether the automated-label gain is conditional on stimulus difficulty and prior AI familiarity, using a preregistered moderator and an adequately powered sample.
hypothesis: H1: automated labels raise d' relative to control (0.035 minimum effect). H2: the label gain is smaller for hard (recent-generator) stimuli. H3: the label gain differs by ai_scale (high vs low familiarity).
primary_outcome: Discernment d' (z(hit rate) minus z(false-alarm rate)) across the 8 posts, with condition by difficulty and condition by ai_scale interaction tests.
comparison: Control vs automated label, crossed within person with stimulus difficulty (older vs recent generator), and moderated by ai_scale (pre-treatment).
unresolved: The actual image and text stimuli, including older vs recent generator outputs, must be supplied by the research team.
The automated label accuracy rate and wording must be fixed by the research team.
Compensation and IRB approval number must be supplied by the research team.
label: Generalizability

title: Discernment vs response bias: manipulating base rates
why: Discriminates the two positions of D1 by separating bias from sensitivity. If interventions work, d' rises under any base rate. If the effects are bias, they vanish or flip when the share of AI items changes.

power_target.basis: H5 observed 0.066-0.091 with SE about 0.03; 300 per cell detects 0.04-0.05 at 80% power.

rationale: The source found Breathing and Nudge raised detection of AI posts without raising recognition of authentic posts (H5 gains 0.066-0.091, SE about 0.03), which fits a bias toward answering AI. Pooled accuracy was only about 1 point (CI -0.3 to 2.4), so it is unclear whether individual interventions help. Changing the share of AI items separates a real sensitivity gain from a shifted answering criterion.
contribution: Tests whether intervention gains persist as d' under both 20% and 80% AI base rates, or vanish or flip as a criterion shift.
hypothesis: If the interventions improve discernment, d' rises relative to control at both base rates and the intervention by base-rate interaction on d' is near zero. If they only bias responses toward answering AI, d' does not differ and c shifts toward AI responses, and this shift shrinks or reverses when 80% of items are AI.
primary_outcome: Signal-detection sensitivity d' per respondent, with criterion c as co-primary, computed from 20 item-level AI/authentic judgments.
comparison: Breathing and Guide vs control on d' and c, within each base rate. Interaction test of intervention by base rate. Optional accuracy-payoff robustness check.
unresolved: The actual image and video files, the guide graphic and the item pools must be supplied by the research team.
IRB approval number and compensation need to be set by the research team.
The remaining 18 item/response pairs must be built from the same template.
label: Theoretical debate
